text: Infosys Limited is an Indian multinational technology company that provides information technology, business consulting, and outsourcing services. Founded in 1981 by seven engineers—N. R. Narayana Murthy, Nandan Nilekani, Kris Gopalakrishnan, S. D. Shibulal, K. Dinesh, N. S. Raghavan, and Ashok Arora—with an initial capital of $250, it was incorporated as Infosys Consultants Private Limited in Pune on 2 July 1981 and later relocated to Bangalore in 1983. Arora left the company in 1989 and sold his shares to the other co-founders. In the 1980s, Infosys briefly produced hardware products such as electronic telex machines and keyboard concentrators. Its core business in offshore custom software development grew after India’s 1991 economic liberalisation. In February 1993, Infosys launched its initial public offering (IPO) at ₹95 per share, which was initially undersubscribed but was "bailed out" by US investment bank Morgan Stanley, which acquired a 13% equity stake at the offer price. Trading began in June 1993 at ₹145 per share. The company released Bancs2000 in 1994, Entark in 1995, and the Y2K toolset "In2000" in 1995. During the mid to late 1990s, it incubated subsidiaries like e-fulfillment, Yantra, and OnMobile, which were later spun off. In March 1999, Infosys listed its American depositary receipts (ADRs) on Nasdaq, becoming the first Indian company to do so, and it was among the top 20 companies by market capitalization on Nasdaq. The ADR listing was later transferred to NYSE Euronext to improve access for European investors. In 1999, Infosys launched Finacle, a core banking software suite replacing Bancs2000, and established SETLabs (later renamed Infosys Labs). In 2004, SETLabs formed an intellectual property (IP) cell, and by 2006, Infosys was reported to earn about 10% of its total revenue from patent-pending IP assets. In 2002, Infosys created Progeon (now Infosys BPM), with Citigroup taking a minority stake for $20 million; in 2006, Infosys bought out Citigroup’s 23% stake for $115 million. In 2009, Infosys established Infosys Public Services in Rockville, Maryland, focusing on federal and state government projects in the US, Canada, and the UK. In 2012, Infosys opened its 18th US office in Milwaukee, primarily to serve Harley-Davidson, and announced hiring over 1,200 employees in 2011 and an additional 2,000 in 2012. In July 2014, Infosys launched EdgeVerve Systems, a subsidiary offering enterprise software in business operations, customer service, procurement, and commerce network domains, and transferred Finacle’s assets to it in August 2015. In 2015, Infosys launched a $500 million Innovation Fund to invest in early-stage startups, including $250 million for Indian startups. In 2018, Infosys formed a 60:40 joint venture with Temasek Holdings in Singapore, named Infosys Compaz (iCompaz), to serve Southeast Asian markets. On 24 August 2021, Infosys became the fourth Indian company to reach a market capitalization of US$100 billion. The company offers software development, maintenance, and independent validation services across industries such as finance, insurance, and manufacturing, with Infosys Consulting providing digital experience, cloud, data analytics, artificial intelligence, engineering, and sustainability services, and Infosys BPM offering outsourcing in finance, procurement, customer service, and HR. Infosys provides digital products and platforms for digital transformation, including Finacle, Panaya, Equinox, Meridian, and Cortex, and offers services in cloud via Cobalt, generative AI via Topaz, and AI marketing via Aster. Its shares are listed on the BSE (as part of the SENSEX) and NSE (as part of the NIFTY 50), and through ADRs on the New York Stock Exchange. The promoter shareholding has steadily declined since June 1993, with further reductions due to the employee stock option scheme and the 1999 ADR listing; the Life Insurance Corporation of India is the largest shareholder. As of 31 March 2024, Infosys operates 94 sales and marketing offices and 139 development centers globally, with operations in India, the US, Canada, China, Australia, Japan, the Middle East, and Europe. In the fiscal year 2023-24, 61% of revenue came from North America, 25% from Europe, 3% from India, and 11% from other regions. Infosys faced scrutiny over its operations in Moscow after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, clarifying it had no active business with Russian firms and that only administrative staff remained by November 2022, handling contract transfers. The Infosys Global Education Centre, located on a 337-acre campus in Mysore, established in 2002, has 400 instructors and over 200 classrooms and trained approximately 125,000 engineering graduates by June 2015, with capacity to train up to 14,000 employees at any time. The Infosys Leadership Institute (ILI) in Mysore trains about 4,000 trainees annually to develop senior leaders for executive roles. As of 31 March 2024, the company employs 317,240 people, known as "Infoscions," with 39.3% being women, and 85% of employees were located in India in 2023. Starting mid-2015, Infosys eliminated its dress code, allowing jeans and casual clothing daily, ending a formal dress code that included a tie for males twice a week since 2008. From 1981 to 2014, the company’s CEOs were its founders, with N. R. Narayana Murthy leading for 21 years; Vishal Sikka was the first external CEO, serving for about three years and resigning in August 2017. UB Pravin Rao served as Interim CEO and Managing Director after Sikka’s departure, and Salil Parekh was appointed CEO and MD effective 2 January 2018. In 2011, Infosys faced visa fraud allegations for using B-1 visas for work requiring H-1B visas, stemming from an internal complaint by an American employee who filed a lawsuit alleging harassment and marginalization, which was dismissed, along with a similar case. These allegations led to investigations by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and a federal grand jury. In October 2013, Infosys settled a civil suit with U.S. authorities by paying $34 million, without admitting guilt, stating it denied claims of systemic visa fraud, misuse, or immigration abuse. In December 2019, Infosys settled a visa and tax fraud case with the State of California for $800,000, involving nearly 500 employees working on B-1 visas between 2006 and 2017 instead of H-1B visas to avoid paying California payroll taxes. In 2013, technical issues arose after Infosys took over the MCA21 portal from Tata Consultancy Services, and similar problems occurred in 2016 after a system migration. In 2020, the finance ministry identified glitches in the GSTN portal, summoning Infosys executives; in 2022, tax professionals raised concerns about technical issues. In 2021, the newly launched Income Tax portal developed by Infosys had multiple glitches, leading to a summons for CEO Salil Parekh, with issues unresolved for months and forcing a deadline extension; in 2022, users continued to report malfunctions on the portal’s first anniversary. In late 2013, Infosys’s plan to install software tracking staff computer time caused employee resentment.
